valid.name: return this (fluent interface)
valid.code: class C { m(): this { return this; } }

valid.name: return of a bare identifier - already a binding
valid.code: function f(value: number): number { return value; }

valid.name: return of a single-hop member expression off this
valid.code: class C { get(): number { return this.count; } private count = 0; }

valid.name: return of a chained member expression - member reads are never flagged, at any depth
valid.code: class C { get(): number { return this.inner.count; } private inner = { count: 0 }; }

valid.name: return of a new expression (construction, not delegation)
valid.code: function f(): Date { return new Date(); }

valid.name: return of an object literal (construction, not delegation)
valid.code: function f(): { a: number } { return { a: 1 }; }

valid.name: return of an array literal (construction, not delegation)
return of a closure (construction, not delegation)
return await - the await keyword already marks the suspension point, 0/26 bound in the survey
valid.code: async function f(): Promise<number> { return await g(); } async function g(): Promise<number> { return 1; }

valid.name: already bound - the point of the rule, not a violation
valid.code: function f(): number { const result = g(); return result; } function g(): number { return 1; }

invalid.name: hazard: unbound call - and no fixer is ever emitted, verified via output: null
hazard: unbound conditional (the exact reported shape - conditional-of-object-literals)
invalid.code: interface R { readonly classification: 'contract' | 'pureData'; } function f(evidence: unknown): R { return evidence === undefined ? { 'classification': 'pureData' } : { 'classification': 'contract' }; }

invalid.name: hazard: unbound logical expression
invalid.code: function f(a: string | undefined, b: string): string { return a || b; }

invalid.name: hazard: unbound binary expression
invalid.code: function f(a: number, b: number): number { return a + b; }

invalid.name: hazard: unbound optional-chained call
invalid.code: function f(g?: () => number): number | undefined { return g?.(); }
